scorecard: 30/30 attacks refused with the expected code
how: Chain attacks are the exact transactions an attacker would send, executed by a Concordium node as dry runs (InvokeInstance, invoker = the attacker): the real contract runs on the current state and returns its refusal code. Nothing is sent and no fee is paid. Re-run: GET /api/proof/attacks?fresh=1.

attacks.title: Pay an invoice that is already paid
attacks.plain: A paid invoice cannot be paid again.

attacks.title: Pay a different amount than the invoice
attacks.plain: The amount must equal the invoice exactly.

attacks.title: Pay an invoice number that does not exist
attacks.plain: Only invoices on the book can be paid.

attacks.title: Seller pays its own invoice (wash / fake volume)
attacks.plain: A seller cannot pay itself.

attacks.title: Payee details changed after the invoice was issued, then the old invoice is paid
attacks.plain: The payee was re-bound after this invoice; the invoice carries the old version, so the chain refuses it (the "changed bank details" fraud).

attacks.title: A strict buyer pays a seller it never approved
attacks.plain: A buyer that set strict mode pays only approved sellers.

attacks.title: Someone else pays an invoice locked to the buyer agent
attacks.plain: An invoice issued to one payer cannot be settled by another account.

attacks.title: Invoice to a lookalike address of the real payee (alias, same first 29 bytes)
attacks.plain: The lookalike 42jaZZ…nUj7e6 is not the bound payee address; an invoice to it is refused.

attacks.title: Invoice to an account that was never proposed
attacks.plain: Only a payee that accepted the binding can be invoiced.

attacks.title: Invoice to a payee that was proposed but never accepted
attacks.plain: Proposing is not enough: the payee must sign the acceptance.

attacks.title: Register an invoice that is already past due (backdated)
attacks.plain: A backdated invoice is refused.

attacks.title: Re-register an existing invoice number with new details
attacks.plain: Invoice numbers cannot be reused.

attacks.title: Register with an agent token that does not exist
attacks.plain: Only a registered CIS-8004 agent can invoice.

attacks.title: An outsider registers an invoice with the seller's agent token
attacks.plain: The agent token belongs to the seller; nobody else can use it.

attacks.title: Accept a payee binding nobody proposed
attacks.plain: An account cannot bind itself as a payee.

attacks.title: Accept a proposal with a different name proof (anchor)
attacks.plain: The payee must accept exactly the proof that was proposed.

attacks.title: Accept an older or newer version of the proposal
attacks.plain: The payee must accept the exact version on the book.

attacks.title: An outsider revokes the real payee's binding (denial of payment)
attacks.plain: Only the seller or the payee can revoke.

attacks.title: Agent records a No-match verdict as its acknowledgment
attacks.plain: Only Match or Close match can be acknowledged.

attacks.title: Agent records Unverified as its acknowledgment
attacks.plain: "Verification not possible" is never payable.

attacks.title: Agent acknowledges a payee version that is not on the book
attacks.plain: The acknowledgment must name the current version.

attacks.title: The payee acknowledges itself on behalf of buyers
attacks.plain: Only a buyer can acknowledge.

attacks.method: finalized refusal re-read from the node
attacks.title: Pay a freshly bound impostor during the cooling-off
attacks.plain: A new payee binding cannot be paid until its cooling-off is over.

attacks.method: finalized refusal re-read from the node
attacks.title: A second payment really sent
attacks.plain: The second payment was sent and refused on chain; nothing moved.

attacks.title: Invoice names the payee "PayOnce Lab" (one letter off)
attacks.plain: A near name is Close match: never paid automatically.

attacks.title: Invoice names "PayOnсe Labs" with a Cyrillic с
attacks.plain: Lookalike characters are not the proven name.

attacks.title: Real name, lookalike address (alias of the real account)
attacks.plain: The name alone never makes an address payable.

attacks.title: Real name claimed by the impostor account
attacks.plain: An account with no name proof is Verification not possible.

attacks.title: Close match paid with a UI click instead of a signed approval
attacks.plain: A Close match needs the payer's wallet signature over the verdict and invoice.

attacks.title: Approval "signed" with a key that is not the payer's
attacks.plain: The signature is checked against the payer account keys on chain.
